Greece planning guide

Planning a corporate event in Greece

Start with what the group needs to do together. Compare Athens, the islands and resort options, then match your headcount and room layout to a venue.

Athens or the islands Venue capacities FAQs

Athens or the islands?

Athens for a meeting-led programme

Start in Athens for a congress, product launch or group arriving from several countries. You can put a plenary and breakouts under one roof, then host a separate dinner in the city or on the Athens Riviera.

Explore Athens →

The islands for an incentive or retreat

Choose Mykonos for time on the water, Santorini for a dinner above the caldera or Corfu for a smaller retreat. For a larger group that also needs meeting space, look at resort options in Crete or Rhodes.

  • Mykonos
  • Santorini
  • Corfu
  • Crete
  • Rhodes

When the programme has two parts

Hold the working sessions in Athens, then move to one island for the incentive. Set aside time for the transfer. If a second flight or ferry would take too much time, consider a Peloponnese resort with meeting space and activities from one base.

Explore the Peloponnese →

Greece event planning FAQs

What works well for an incentive trip in Greece?

For a short trip, pick one base and build around a shared experience: an evening overlooking the Acropolis, a sailing day in the Cyclades, or a meal among the olive groves in the Peloponnese. A longer programme gives you room for a city and an island without spending too much of the trip in transit.

When should we hold a corporate event in Greece?

April to June and September to October are good starting points for outdoor programmes. July and August are busy, particularly on the islands, so allow more lead time for rooms and transport. Athens is a practical option for indoor events in winter. Check island flights, ferries and venue openings for your dates.

How do we choose between Athens and an island?

Start with Athens if your programme needs a large plenary, several breakout rooms or simple arrivals from multiple countries. Choose an island if the main purpose is an incentive or retreat. Crete and Rhodes can also work for larger groups that want a resort with meeting facilities.

Can Mykonos or Santorini work for a large group?

For a private dinner or an incentive built around one venue, 50–150 guests is a useful starting range. For 200 or more, check room blocks, coach access and where everyone can meet or dine together. Crete, Rhodes, Athens and the Peloponnese offer more options when keeping the whole group in one place is essential.

How should we plan airport and ferry transfers?

Book group vehicles ahead, especially in summer. Share the arrival manifest and luggage requirements so transfers can be scheduled around each flight or sailing. For a programme split between Athens and an island, leave a buffer for delays and keep a backup plan for weather-dependent activities.

Which Athens venues can seat more than 1,000 people?

Megaron lists 1,960 fixed seats in its Christos Lambrakis Hall. The Athenaeum Ballroom at InterContinental can seat up to 1,500 theatre-style. A stage, production desks and accessibility requirements can change the usable capacity.

What does a destination management company handle locally?

A DMC can shortlist venues, coordinate site visits and suppliers, plan transport and activities, and manage delivery on site. The local team also checks practical details such as vehicle access, setup time and wet-weather alternatives before you commit to the programme.

Can our company book directly with One Event?

Yes. Send your dates or date range, headcount, event goals and any requirements for accommodation, plenary space or activities. If you already have a budget range, include it so the first shortlist reflects what you can spend.
